bugs.why: When the buffered data is an exact multiple of chunk_size, remainder is 0 and `value[-0:]` is the whole buffer, so all already-returned bytes are re-buffered and emitted again.

agent.explanation: When remainder is 0, value[-remainder:] becomes value[-0:], which slices the entire value and writes it back into the buffer instead of clearing it.
agent.fix:
self._buffer.seek(0)
        self._buffer.write(value[-remainder:] if remainder else b"")
        self._buffer.truncate()

bugs.why: In the qop-less (RFC 2069) branch digest_data already starts with HA1, so prefixing HA1 again yields digest(HA1:HA1:nonce:HA2) and authentication fails.

agent.explanation: When qop is None (legacy RFC 2069 mode), digest_data includes HA1 as its first element. Joining key_digest with HA1 again results in HA1 being duplicated (HA1:HA1:nonce:HA2), producing an incorrect digest response.

filtered.explanation: When qop is None (legacy RFC 2069 mode), digest_data includes HA1 as its first element. Joining key_digest with HA1 again results in HA1 being duplicated (HA1:HA1:nonce:HA2), producing an incorrect digest response.

bugs.why: Returning early skips the shared `cert` handling below, so a client certificate passed with verify=False is silently never loaded.

agent.explanation: Returning early when `verify=False` bypasses the subsequent `if cert:` block, preventing client certificates from being loaded when server verification is disabled.
agent.fix:
ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT)
        ctx.check_hostname = False
        ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE

bugs.why: typeof null is "object" and the null check now runs after this line, so getParsedType(null) throws a TypeError reading `then` of null instead of returning "null".
`value or None` turns an explicit empty value like `--name=` into None, so the parser consumes the next argument as the value (or errors) instead of using the empty string.
re.ASCII is passed as the positional `count` argument of re.sub, not as flags, so the ASCII flag is not applied.

agent.explanation: Passing re.ASCII as the fourth positional argument to re.sub specifies the count parameter, not flags, which causes an exception or incorrect substitution behavior.

bugs.why: The Expires difference is in milliseconds but is compared against a limit in seconds, so any Expires more than ~9.6 hours ahead throws.

agent.explanation: MAX_COOKIE_AGE_SECONDS is in seconds (34560000), but opt.expires.getTime() - Date.now() returns milliseconds, causing the check to compare seconds against milliseconds and incorrectly allow expiration dates far into the future.

bugs.why: maxBodySize is now enforced only via the client-supplied Content-Length header; a chunked request (no Content-Length, Number(undefined) is NaN) or an understated length streams an unbounded body because onData no longer counts bytes.
The promise returned by .finally() is no longer caught, so whenever a tracked operation rejects it produces an extra unhandled rejection that Vitest reports as an error.
